assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and current fungal nomenclature records retain Mortierella as genus NCBITaxon:4855 and Index Fungorum/MycoBank record 20345, with Mortierella polycephala as type species. Current evidence supports mainly coenocytic, irregularly septate hyphae and simple or branched sporangiophores with globose terminal sporangia. The reconstruction is type-species anchored, representative, non-universal, and non-diagnostic.
assets.visualReview: One connected hyphal specimen grouping supports exactly three simple upright main sporangiophores and three smooth, closed, globose terminal sporangia. Numerous round spore-like bodies are visibly contained within each continuous outer sporangial boundary; none protrudes or appears as an external beaded cluster. No released spore cloud is visible. Eleven distinct transverse tonal seams remain visible along the basal hyphae, excluding branching junctions and strand crossings; this exceeds the prompt target of no more than two and is an accepted output-specific feature, not a universal septation claim. The wide basal network extends beyond the standard cover-safe vertical crop but is not clipped by the source canvas. No conidiophore brush, macroconidium, text, label, scale bar, substrate, plant, host material, scene, signature, or watermark is visible.
